title: Councillor calls on Rochdale Council to scrap its climate targets and focus on the cost of living
excerpt: A motion from Cllr John Taylor asks Rochdale's full council to rescind the borough's 2038 carbon-neutral pledge and put the cost-of-living crisis and housing emergency first.
image_alt: Illustration: Rochdale, environment. Not a photograph of the event.

corrections.note: Corrected on 12 November 2026: an earlier version said the full council meeting was on 13 October. The source gave the meeting as the following Thursday and did not state a date, so the date has been removed.

body:
A Rochdale councillor has asked the borough's full council to scrap its climate emergency targets and put helping residents through the cost-of-living crisis first.

The motion from Cllr John Taylor was due to be considered at a meeting of Rochdale's full council.

In 2019 the council passed a climate emergency motion, pledging to make both the council's operations and the wider borough carbon neutral by 2038.

Cllr Taylor's motion says: “Since 2019 it has become clear that our local impact on carbon reduction is negligible and it does not represent the most efficient use of our resources.”

It adds that the cost-of-living crisis and housing emergency “must be our strategic priorities alongside the efficient and effective delivery of our core services”, and that future efforts to achieve carbon neutrality “must also be cost neutral”.

The motion notes that a local repeal would not override national law, under which the UK remains bound by the Climate Change Act to reach net zero by 2050. It also asks the council to stop any climate programme that cannot show a “clear resident benefit, financial saving or statutory requirement”.

The same meeting was due to hear updates on expanding the electric vehicle charging network and on the Rochdale Town Centre Heat Network, which will use heat from sewers to cut energy costs. The council has received a £1 million commercialisation grant from the Government and will tender for a development partner for the scheme.
